newsitem.title: LEBANON: Iraqi athletes halted at Lebanon border.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi athletes halted at Lebanon border.

text.p: A 97-member Iraqi athletic team were halted at the Lebanese-Syrian crossing point of Masnaa' on Friday and will not be granted visas to take part in the eighth Pan Arab Games which open on Saturday, an official said.
Three buses bearing posters of President Saddam Hussein and signs reading "The Iraqi delegation to the Arab Games" and "Iraq's national team" were parked outside the border offices in Masnaa'.
Athletes in blue uniforms waited in the buses while the head of the delegation ,Assil Tabari ,was admitted to the offices of the general security.
A Lebanese general security border officer told Reuters: "No visas for the delegation".
Lebanon decided to exclude Iraq after Kuwait and Saudi Arabia threatened to boycott the games if Iraq participated.
Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have maintained a hawkish stand on Iraq since the Gulf War which followed Iraq's invasion of Kuwait but other Gulf Arab states have softened their line.
Iraq was among 20 countries due to take part in the two-week games.

Lebanon, which has close ties with Kuwait, severed diplomatic ties with Baghdad in 1994 after the murder of an Iraqi dissident in Beirut. Four Iraqi diplomats suspected of involvement in the slaying were held in jail for three years. One of them died in jail.
